en: Ali ibn Khashram narrated to us: Isa—meaning Ibn Yunus—informed us, from Shu'bah, from Simak ibn Harb, from Alqamah ibn Wa'il, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Do not say 'al-karm', but say 'al-habalah'"—meaning grapes.

Ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which was: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should call grapes 'al-karm'; indeed, 'al-karm' is the Muslim man."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Ali ibn Hafs narrated to us: Warqa' narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should say 'al-karm'; for indeed, 'al-karm' is the heart of the believer."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Do not name grapes 'al-karm', for 'al-karm' is the Muslim man."

Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Do not say 'karm'; for indeed, al-karm is the heart of the believer."

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should revile time, for Allah is time. And none of you should call grapes 'al-karm', for 'al-karm' is the Muslim man."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Do not revile time, for Allah is time."

Qutaybah narrated to us: al-Mughirah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should say: 'Woe to time!' for Allah is time."

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, said: 'The son of Adam offends Me by saying: "Woe to time!" So let none of you say: "Woe to time!" For I am time; I alternate its night and day, and whenever I wish, I take them away.'"

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Abi Umar narrated it to us—and the wording is that of Ibn Abi Umar; Ishaq said: informed us, and Ibn Abi Umar said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, said: 'The son of Adam offends Me by reviling time, while I am time; I alternate the night and the day.'"

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, saying: Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, said: 'The son of Adam reviles time, while I am time; in My Hand are the night and the day.'"

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "While a dog was circling a well, about to die of thirst, a prostitute from the prostitutes of the Children of Israel saw it. She took off her leather shoe, drew water with it for the dog, and gave it to drink; so she was forgiven on account of that."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "A prostitute saw a dog on a hot day circling a well, lolling its tongue out because of thirst. So she drew water for it with her leather sock, and she was forgiven."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from what was recited to him, from Sumayy, the freed slave of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "While a man was walking along a path, he became severely thirsty. He found a well, went down into it, and drank. Then he came out, and behold, there was a dog panting and eating moist earth out of thirst. The man said: 'This dog has reached the same extremity of thirst that I had reached.' So he went down into the well, filled his leather sock with water, and held it in his mouth until he climbed up, and gave the dog to drink. Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there really a reward for us in serving these animals?" He said: "In every living being with a moist liver, there is a reward."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of their hadith.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—Abd said: informed us, and Ibn Rafi' said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, who said: al-Zuhri said: and Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), in the sense of the hadith of Hisham ibn Urwah.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (Second chain) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, with this chain of transmission. And in both their hadiths: "she tied it up." And in the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah: "the vermin of the earth."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A woman was punished because of a cat: she neither fed it nor gave it drink, nor did she leave it free to eat from the vermin of the earth."

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated it to me: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A woman was punished because of a cat she tied up: she neither fed it nor gave it drink, nor did she let it eat from the vermin of the earth."

Harun ibn Abdillah and Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Yahya ibn Khalid narrated to me, both from Ma'n ibn Isa, from Malik ibn Anas, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), in the sense of the hadith of Juwayriyah.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma' ibn Ubayd al-Duba'i narrated to me: Juwayriyah—meaning Ibn Asma'—narrated to us, from Nafi', from Abdullah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A woman was punished because of a cat that she imprisoned until it died, and thus she entered the Fire because of it: she neither fed it nor gave it drink when she confined it, nor did she leave it free to eat from the vermin of the earth."
Harun ibn Abdillah and Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated it to us, from Ma'n ibn Isa, from Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with that.

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to me: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, and from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the like of its meaning.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma' al-Duba'i narrated to me: Juwayriyah ibn Asma' narrated to us, from Nafi', from Abdullah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A woman was punished because of a cat that she imprisoned until it died, and thus she entered the Fire because of it: she neither fed it nor gave it drink when she confined it, nor did she leave it free to eat from the vermin of the earth."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which was: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "One of the prophets descended to camp under a tree, and an ant bit him. So he commanded his luggage to be brought out from underneath it, and ordered the tree to be burnt in the fire. He said: Then Allah revealed to him: 'Why not only one ant?'"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Mughirah—meaning Ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "One of the prophets descended to rest under a tree, and an ant bit him. He ordered that his belongings be taken out from beneath it, then ordered it to be burned; whereupon Allah revealed to him: 'Why not just a single ant?'"

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "An ant bit one of the prophets, so he ordered that the colony of ants be burned. Whereupon Allah revealed to him: 'Just because an ant bit you, you destroyed a whole community among the communities that glorifies Allah?'"

Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Zakariyya—narrated to us, from Suhayl: my sister narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "For the first blow, seventy good deeds."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us; (Second chain) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us; (Third chain) and Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Zakariyya—narrated to us; (Fourth chain) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan; all of them from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), in the sense of the hadith of Khalid from Suhayl, except Jarir alone, for in his hadith it says: "Whoever kills a gecko with the first blow, one hundred good deeds are recorded for him, with the second blow less than that, and with the third blow less than that."
